tools.name: doctrine
tools.description: Vigi-Sky identity and method: never 'UFO detected', Hatch vs live corpus, book ISBN, founder.

tools.name: cite
tools.description: Map a user question to the best Vigi-Sky (or GEIPAN) URL to cite.

tools.name: aurora
tools.description: Live Kp/aurora odds from Vigi-Sky (NOAA) plus France Kp 6/7/8–9 thresholds.

tools.name: iss_passes
tools.description: Upcoming bright satellite/ISS passes from a lat/lon (SGP4), ISS first. Default night_only=true: only passes in a dark sky with the satellite sunlit. For a French/European city by name use iss_city_passes.

tools.name: identify
tools.description: Match a timed azimuth/elevation to known bright satellites. Verdict: compatible | no_catalog_match | insufficient_data. Never 'UFO detected'.

tools.name: nearby_cases
tools.description: Historical Hatch UDB cases near a point. Archive 1900–2002, approximate geocode — not live Vigi-Sky reports.

tools.name: first_skies
tools.description: Query Ciel des peuples: 9 named nations, asterisms with RA/Dec, sources, attested vs interpretation vs reserved. nation=dine | q=pléiades | western=orion | theme=agriculture | lat=44 for horizon honesty. Never 'the Indians'.

tools.name: tonight_sky
tools.description: Kp + next potentially visible satellite pass + First Skies asterisms. Default night_only=true (no daylight ISS).

tools.name: observation_conditions
tools.description: Night/moon/solar observing-conditions score. NOT a UFO-appearance probability.

tools.name: solar
tools.description: Live solar/CME context plus current Kp from Vigi-Sky APIs.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Vigi-Sky API health, Hatch archive size, public observation counts.

tools.name: hatch_stats
tools.description: Hatch UDB stats (decades, countries) + wiki lessons. Archive, not live 2026.

tools.name: hatch_search
tools.description: Filter Hatch cases near a point by country/text. Approximate geocode.

tools.name: nasa_apod
tools.description: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day via Vigi-Sky.

tools.name: neo_watch
tools.description: Near-Earth objects for today (astronomy, not UAP).

tools.name: starlink_trains
tools.description: Recently launched Starlink trains (count + launch id).

tools.name: nights_network
tools.description: Public Sentinel night reports. Currently empty — says so honestly.

tools.name: object_lookup
tools.description: Quick Messier/deep-sky hint. q is required (M31, M42, M45…). No silent default.

tools.name: hypothesis_rank
tools.description: Rank cheap natural hypotheses from a free-text sighting. No origin claim.

tools.name: capabilities
tools.description: Map of this public MCP + the shipped local vigisky-sentinel (23 typed tools, stdio/127.0.0.1).

tools.name: iss_city_passes
tools.description: When will the ISS (and Tiangong, Starlink trains) be visible over a city? Next visible passes for 41 French, Belgian, Swiss, UK and Irish cities, with direction. The calendar subscription (webcal) alerts 10 minutes before each pass. Give city, or lat/lon for the nearest covered city.

tools.name: what_did_i_see
tools.description: Identify a light seen in the sky, even afterwards: ISS, Tiangong, bright satellites, Starlink trains, planets, Moon, bright stars. Give place and time; direction (az) and moving=true/false sharpen the answer. Never 'UFO detected'.

tools.name: which_star
tools.description: Which star or planet is that? Bright stars, planets and the Moon closest to a direction (azimuth, elevation) at a place and time.

tools.name: sky_events
tools.description: Live sky events explained: predicted bright ISS passes and Starlink trains (48 h), and groups of witness reports with the tested explanation (compatible / contradicted / untestable / under review). No personal data.

tools.name: moon
tools.description: Moon phase and illuminated fraction at a time (default now), next full and new Moon, and what it means for observing.

tools.name: triangulate
tools.description: Estimate the height and distance of an object seen at the same moment by 2 to 6 witnesses, from each witness position and line of sight (azimuth, elevation). Gives a height range for compass errors. A candidate, never a proof.

tools.name: eclipse_2027
tools.description: Total solar eclipse of 2 August 2027 (Spain, Morocco, Egypt…): total or partial at a place, magnitude, contact times (local time for 830 cities), duration of totality, Sun height.

tools.name: asteroid_impact
tools.description: What if an asteroid hit? Energy, air burst or crater, blast/heat/earthquake radii and effects at a distance (Collins, Melosh & Marcus 2005), plus how often such an object hits Earth.

tools.name: hawking_black_hole
tools.description: Stephen Hawking's black hole numbers for any mass: horizon radius, Hawking temperature, entropy, evaporation time.

tools.name: drake_equation
tools.description: Drake equation and the Fermi paradox: N for your factors, and the probability we are alone once uncertainty is honest (Sandberg, Drexler & Ord 2018).

tools.name: proposer_signalement
tools.description: Etape 1 de 2 : prepare un brouillon de signalement d'observation (jamais une detection). Ne publie rien et n'envoie rien. Renvoie un resume a montrer au temoin, un jeton, et l'explication immediate si lieu et heure sont donnes.

tools.name: confirmer_action
tools.description: Etape 2 de 2 : transmet le signalement a Vigi-Sky (station Temoin) et previent l'equipe. N'appeler qu'apres l'accord explicite du temoin dans la conversation, apres lui avoir montre le resume.

tools.name: annuler_action
tools.description: Annule un brouillon de signalement non confirme et efface ses donnees.

tools.name: statut_actions
tools.description: Compteurs des ecritures preparees et plafonds (aucune donnee personnelle).

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "iss_passes" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Upcoming bright satellite/ISS passes (SGP4). night_only=true keeps only dark+sunlit passes." → after: "Upcoming bright satellite/ISS passes from a lat/lon (SGP4), ISS first. Default night_only=true: only passes in a dark sky with the satellite sunlit. For a French/European city by name use iss_city_passes."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
